summary: Egypt issues a 30-day tourist eVisa through its official portal visa2egypt.gov.eg (25 USD single entry, 60 USD multiple entry) and sells the same visa on arrival for 25 USD cash to a broad list of nationalities, including the US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia and Japan; visitors flying directly to the Sinai Red Sea resorts can instead use a free 15-day Sinai-only entry stamp.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival in Egypt.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required if you arrive from, or transited more than 12 hours through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — including much of sub-Saharan Africa and South America.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but medical cover is strongly recommended — private hospitals in tourist areas expect payment or proof of insurance up front.

onwardTicket.text: Onward travel is not systematically checked at the border, but airlines and the eVisa application may ask for return or onward ticket details and accommodation information.

proofOfFunds.text: There is no published fixed amount, but border officers may ask travellers to show sufficient means of support for the intended stay.

declarations.name: Paper arrival card
declarations.submitWindow: On the plane or at the border before immigration
declarations.text: Egypt still uses a short paper arrival card, handed out on the plane or available at the immigration hall — fill in your passport details and address in Egypt before joining the queue.

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency above 10,000 USD (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure. Import and export of Egyptian pounds is limited to 5,000 EGP.

notes: Drones are banned in Egypt without a hard-to-get military permit — do not bring one, even packed away; they are confiscated and travellers have been detained.
Exporting antiquities or anything that looks like one is a serious criminal offence — buy souvenirs from licensed shops and keep receipts.
Satellite phones and some radio equipment require prior authorisation.

payments.text: Cards work in hotels, resort restaurants and larger shops, but Egypt runs on cash: bazaars, taxis, site entrance extras and tips (baksheesh) all need small notes. ATMs are common in cities and resorts — carry small-denomination pounds.

safety.text: Main tourist areas (Cairo, Luxor, Aswan, the Nile Valley and Red Sea resorts) are heavily policed and generally safe for visitors, but avoid the North Sinai governorate and the Western Desert near the Libyan border, and expect security checkpoints when travelling between cities.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Egypt Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: October to April brings mild, sunny weather ideal for the pyramids and Nile Valley sites; summer is extremely hot inland, though Red Sea resorts stay busy year-round.

tips.text: Apply for the Egyptian eVisa only at the official portal visa2egypt.gov.eg — look-alike sites charge large markups on the 25 USD fee and sometimes deliver nothing.
Drones are illegal to bring into Egypt without a military permit, even packed in luggage — they are confiscated at the airport and can lead to detention.

Flying directly to Sharm El Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba or Taba and staying in South Sinai? You can get a free 15-day Sinai-only entry stamp instead of a visa — but it does not cover Cairo, Luxor or diving trips to Ras Mohammed by boat, so most excursion-takers still buy the full visa.

Never photograph military installations, checkpoints or bridges — cameras and phones can be seized. Small tips (baksheesh) are a routine part of daily life for guides, drivers and washroom attendants; keep 5–20 EGP notes handy.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Egypt?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a 30-day tourist visa, obtainable either as an eVisa at visa2egypt.gov.eg (25 USD single entry, 60 USD multiple entry) or on arrival for 25 USD cash at the airport bank counters before immigration. Both grant the same 30-day stay.

faq.question: Is Egypt's visa on arrival better than the eVisa?
faq.answer: They cost the same (25 USD) and grant the same 30-day stay. The eVisa avoids queueing at the airport bank counter and is safer if your airline checks visas before boarding; the visa on arrival needs cash in USD, EUR or GBP. Both are limited to the same list of eligible nationalities.

faq.question: What is the free Sinai entry stamp?
faq.answer: Travellers arriving directly at Sharm El Sheikh, Taba or other South Sinai airports can get a free entry stamp allowing 15 days in the South Sinai resorts (Sharm, Dahab, Nuweiba, Taba) without a visa. It does not allow travel to Cairo, Luxor or the rest of Egypt — for that you need the regular 30-day visa.

faq.question: How long must my passport be valid to enter Egypt?
faq.answer: At least 6 months from your date of arrival. Airlines enforce this at check-in, so renew your passport first if you are close to the limit.

faq.question: Do I need vaccinations for Egypt?
faq.answer: No vaccinations are required for arrivals from Europe, the Americas or most of Asia. A yellow fever certificate (ICVP) is required only if you arrive from or transited through a yellow fever risk country, such as much of sub-Saharan Africa or South America.
